newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Feb 14.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
- China's top legislators are to hold 24th session of standing committee of National People's Congress from February 19 to 25.
- Northwest Qinghai province attracts 670 million yuan ($81 million) of investment from 14 eastern provinces in 1996, up 8.0 percent from 1995.
- China realized 150 billion yuan in industrial output in January, up 10.3 percent from the year-ago month
- China plans to spend 2.8 billion yuan ($337 million) in relocation of population in Three Gorges Dam area this year.
- Ministry of Water Resources says China spent 32.2 billion yuan in construction of water conservancy works since last winter.
- Zhou Xiaochuan, head of State Administration of Foreign Exchange, tells international meeting that China's management of foreign exchange reserves is not for profit
- Central bank Sichuan branch recalls 294 million yuan in loans in interest in 1996
- Customs seize 3,600 tonnes of magnesium intended to be smuggled out of China
- Ao Huicheng, vice-director of central bank capital planning department, says bank to issue guidelines in credit policy and to boost investment in farm sector
- State Education Commission will place more emphasis on expanding worldwide cross-university exchanges, sending more scholars to study abroad and receiving more foreign students
- Afforestation and water and soil erosion control efforts are under way in Three Gorges Dam area and along the Yangtze River
- China says prisons succeed in reforming inmates
